set.reason: Negative-power reciprocals are explicitly reused in the criteria.
set.scope: Negative exponents as reciprocals

set.reason: The square-root-to-half-power rewrite needs even-root meaning and real-domain restrictions.
set.scope: Rewriting radicals and their meaningful domain

set.reason: The specified aligned-place calculation includes the same column-addition/carry principle as whole-number written addition. Only that shared algorithm component is required.
set.scope: column alignment and carrying in decimal sums

set.reason: The positive-integer case motivates adding exponents through counting factors. The general real law can be learned and applied as a stated rule, so the special case is customary preparation.
set.scope: integer special case of the product law

set.reason: Rational exponents give concrete instances and motivate the negative-base cautions. Applying the general laws to symbolic real exponents does not require evaluating radicals as fractional powers.
set.scope: rational exponents as precursor to real exponents

set.reason: Seeing a^x as an exponential function supports thinking of exponents as continuous real inputs. The algebraic laws and domain checks can be applied without classifying function families.
set.scope: interpreting positive-base powers as functions of real inputs

set.reason: Arbitrary real exponents, including irrational ones, and the positive-real-base restriction both presuppose the real number system. The node's scope cannot be stated without it.
set.scope: real exponents and positive-base domain

criteria: Apply power laws with arbitrary real exponents and positive bases.
Distinguish these laws from unsafe negative-base real-power manipulations.
